title: Price Action Analysis Toolkit Development (Part 86): Validating the Entire Sample Library
text:
Contents
Introduction
Designing library-wide validation
MQL5 implementation
Operating and reviewing the batch
Testing
Conclusion
Introduction
The visual reviewer developed in
Part 85
made a stored validation result easier to understand. A sample could be selected, validated, and displayed on its historical chart, where the two lows, the neckline, and the decisive candle were drawn from the validator's own indices. That approach remains useful when the purpose is to study one formation closely.
Individual review requires selecting and validating each sample separately. That is useful for inspecting a formation, but it does not provide a count of the statuses across the stored collection. A batch action supplies this collection view while leaving detailed chart inspection available.
The new
VALIDATE ALL
control copies the in-memory collection. It applies the existing double-bottom validator to every sample and counts the four outcomes. The run also writes a CSV report. It includes the timestamp, validator settings, totals, and one detailed result row per sample. The original
SAMPLE_<ID>.csv
files are not edited.
After this change, the trader can see how the stored examples are distributed across the four statuses. The developer receives one detailed row for every sample, including the selected indices, measurements, and reason. Individual chart review remains available when one of those rows needs to be examined against its candles.
Designing library-wide validation
Two questions, two controls
VALIDATE SELECTED
and
VALIDATE ALL
remain separate. The first answers, "
What did the validator find in this sample
?" It retains the selected sample and result so
SHOW ON CHART
can reconstruct the formation. The second answers, "
How did the current rule set classify the stored collection
?" It processes every record and produces totals plus a CSV report.
Combining the two actions would make the interface less clear. A batch run may contain several confirmed results, but
SHOW ON CHART
can display only one sample at a time. It would be misleading to let a collection result behave like a retained chart subject. When
VALIDATE ALL
is pressed, the panel discards the retained individual result and requests removal of its drawing. If cleanup fails, the batch does not start. Otherwise, the result area displays the collection totals after validation completes. A sample must be selected and validated again before it can be shown on the chart.
The totals do not replace chart inspection. They identify the records worth opening, while the visual reviewer shows whether the selected lows and neckline agree with the intended formation.
Recording the settings with the results
A status has meaning only in relation to the settings that produced it. With a pivot strength of two, a candle must satisfy one local-low definition. Changing the strength changes the candidates available to the pair evaluator. Minimum separation, maximum low difference, required depth, symmetry, breakout buffer, and failure tolerance can also change the final classification.
The report stores the active settings, report schema, sample format and validator revision alongside the results. Floating-point settings use seventeen significant digits. Repeating a classification also requires the same source samples and validator implementation; the report alone does not contain the full candle arrays. Sample IDs identify records within the library, while a separate filename distinguishes each saved run. The source SAMPLE_<ID>.csv files remain unchanged.
Reusing the tested validator
The batch coordinator does not contain a second definition of a double bottom. It calls
ValidateDoubleBottom
() for each stored sample. The mandatory geometry rules, pair search, score, and decisive-close classification therefore remain identical to individual validation.
Using one function avoids maintaining two rule implementations. Matching single and batch results still requires identical candle data, settings and validator code, with both calls completing successfully. A comparison should therefore check the selected indices and measurements as well as the status.
Figure 1. Individual and library-wide validation using the same rule engine.
The coordinator has a narrower responsibility: obtain the collection, validate each element, update status counters, and pass the completed arrays to the CSV writer. It does not inspect chart objects, navigate through history, or calculate alternative measurements.
Stable IDs instead of assumed positions
Sample IDs do not need to be consecutive. A deleted record leaves a gap, and the library does not renumber later samples because the ID is also part of the persistent filename. Renumbering would weaken references made in notes, screenshots, and earlier reports.
Batch validation works on the array returned by
GetAllSamples
(). It never loops from ID 1 to the sample count or constructs guessed filenames. A deletion gap therefore has no effect on the records included in the run: the library, not an assumed numeric sequence, defines the batch.
Stored candles, not the current chart
Every
SPatternSample
contains its symbol, timeframe, and complete candle array. Structural validation uses those stored candles. The chart on which the panel is attached does not provide replacement prices for a batch run.
Because validation uses stored candles, the pattern library can include multiple markets and timeframes. Chart context is required only when
SHOW ON CHART
attempts to draw a selected result. Batch computation and visualization therefore have different context requirements.
Structuring the CSV report
Three sections in one CSV:
The UTF-8 CSV uses explicit
SECTION
,
SUMMARY
,
SECTION
,
SETTINGS
and
SECTION
,
RESULTS
records. Each section has its own header and column count. The results section has 23 columns and one row per sample. A parser must process these sections separately rather than treating the whole file as one rectangular table.
The first section gives the collection totals. The second shows the rules that produced them. The third provides enough detail to investigate why each sample received its status. Keeping the three sections together prevents the settings from being separated from their results.
The report begins with these batch fields:
BATCH_TIME
: records the last known server time read after the validation loop, including seconds. It is not local terminal time, a unique run identifier or the time when report saving completed. Without new quotes, this server timestamp may remain unchanged.
PATTERN_TYPE
: stores the text
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE. REPORT_SCHEMA
,
VALIDATOR_REVISION
and
SAMPLE_FORMAT
identify the report and validation contracts; TIME_BASIS describes the timestamp.
TOTAL
: records the number of samples processed.
INVALID
,
CANDIDATE
,
CONFIRMED
and
FAILED
: record the status counts.
The settings section stores pivot strength, minimum low separation, maximum low difference, minimum depth, minimum symmetry, breakout buffer, and failure tolerance. These values are written from the same
SDoubleBottomSettings
structure passed to each validation call.
The result table starts with sample identity and context: ID, symbol, timeframe, start time, end time, and candle count. It then stores status, score, selected indices, prices, and the validator's reason. An
INVALID
row keeps index values at -1 when no accepted structure exists. This is preferable to inserting plausible coordinates that were never selected.
Separate reports for each run
Reports are saved in
MQL5\Files\PatternLibrary\DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE
with names beginning
VALIDATION_SUMMARY_
. A local date/time and a per-run counter distinguish filenames; the writer rejects a collision instead of overwriting an existing report. The local filename timestamp is separate from the server-based
BATCH_TIME
field.
The writer creates a temporary file, checks the byte count and flush diagnostics, closes it, then reopens it and compares every byte with the intended UTF-8 payload. Only a matching file is renamed to its final CSV name. Error messages identify the failed operation and include an available diagnostic code. Possible causes include paths, permissions, storage problems and file locks.
This is an immediate readback check, not a guarantee against later modification or power loss. A failed temporary-file cleanup is reported. The Experts log records the final report path after a successful export. Earlier reports remain available for comparison; source sample files are not rewritten.
Preserving numerical precision
Report serialization uses seventeen significant digits for settings, prices, scores and measurements. It does not query
SYMBOL_DIGITS
or use the digits of the chart hosting the panel. Export therefore does not require the sample symbol to be available in Market Watch.
The purpose is to retain the calculated double values for later comparison. Some decimals may display binary floating-point tails, and scientific notation may appear for extreme magnitudes. A spreadsheet can apply shorter display formatting without changing the exported file. Precision here concerns serialization; it does not establish the accuracy of the source quotes or the validity of a formation.
System architecture
Part 86 adds
DoubleBottomBatchValidator.mqh
and extends the existing panel. The library, single-sample validator, renderer, and storage modules retain their previous responsibilities.
The panel initiates the action and displays the final totals. The batch module coordinates the run.
CPatternLibrary
supplies actual stored samples, including non-consecutive IDs.
ValidateDoubleBottom
() evaluates each sample with the active settings. The batch writer then creates the consolidated CSV in the pattern folder.
Figure 2. Batch-validation flow from the stored library to panel totals and a consolidated CSV report.
The panel receives only the totals needed on the chart. The CSV receives the detailed sample rows. Neither output changes the source sample files.
MQL5 implementation
The completed project contains nine source files. Eight continue the recorder, validator, and visual reviewer. The new batch module owns collection-wide processing and report creation. The excerpts below follow the execution path from the summary contract to the panel event. The attachment contains the complete compile-ready source tree.
1. Declaring the batch summary
The summary separates completion of validation from completion of export.
validation_complete
becomes true only after every sample has been evaluated and counted.
report_file
remains empty until a verified report has been published. A failed export can therefore leave usable totals without producing a save-success message.
#define
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_REPORT_SCHEMA
"1"
#define
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_VALIDATOR_REVISION
"P86-1"
//--- Separates completed validation from successful report publication
struct
SDoubleBottomBatchSummary
  {
datetime
generated_at;
bool
validation_complete;
int
total;
int
invalid_count;
int
candidate_count;
int
confirmed_count;
int
failed_count;
string
report_file;
  };
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Resets the counts and report state before a batch                |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
void
InitDoubleBottomBatchSummary(SDoubleBottomBatchSummary &summary)
  {
   summary.generated_at =
0
;
   summary.validation_complete =
false
;
   summary.total =
0
;
   summary.invalid_count =
0
;
   summary.candidate_count =
0
;
   summary.confirmed_count =
0
;
   summary.failed_count =
0
;
   summary.report_file =
""
;
  }
2. Preparing storage and counting statuses
The report uses the candidate folder shared by the recorder and reviewer. All four known statuses are counted explicitly. An unknown value returns false instead of being hidden inside the
INVALID
total.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Creates the report directory without changing source records     |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
PrepareDoubleBottomSummaryFolder(
string
&error)
  {
string
folders[
2
];
   folders[
0
] = STORAGE_FOLDER;
   folders[
1
] = GetPatternFolder(PATTERN_DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE);
for
(
int
i =
0
; i <
2
; i++)
     {
ResetLastError
();
if
(!
FolderCreate
(folders[i]))
        {
int
code =
GetLastError
();
if
(code !=
ERR_FILE_IS_DIRECTORY
)
           {
            error =
"Cannot create report folder. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(code);
return
(
false
);
           }
        }
     }
return
(
true
);
  }
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Counts only explicitly recognized validation states              |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
CountDoubleBottomBatchStatus(
const
ENUM_DOUBLE_BOTTOM_STATUS status,
                                  SDoubleBottomBatchSummary &summary)
  {
switch
(status)
     {
case
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_INVALID:   summary.invalid_count++;
return
(
true
);
case
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE: summary.candidate_count++;
return
(
true
);
case
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CONFIRMED: summary.confirmed_count++;
return
(
true
);
case
DOUBLE_BOTTOM_FAILED:    summary.failed_count++;
return
(
true
);
     }
return
(
false
);
  }
The following helpers preserve numeric precision and quote textual fields, including commas, quotation marks and embedded line breaks.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Preserves seventeen significant digits without symbol metadata   |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
string
DoubleBottomBatchNumber(
const
double
value)
  {
return
(
StringFormat
(
"%.17g"
, value));
  }
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Quotes a CSV field, including embedded commas and line breaks    |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
string
QuoteDoubleBottomBatchCsvField(
const
string
value)
  {
string
escaped = value;
StringReplace
(escaped,
"\""
,
"\"\""
);
return
(
"\""
+ escaped +
"\""
);
  }
3. Writing the CSV report
Before opening a file, the writer checks completion state, parallel array sizes and status totals. It recounts the result rows and rejects unknown statuses or recorded execution errors.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Rejects mismatched arrays, unknown states and inconsistent totals|
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
CheckDoubleBottomBatchRows(SPatternSample &samples[],
                                SDoubleBottomValidation &results[],
const
SDoubleBottomBatchSummary &summary,
string
&error)
  {
int
count =
ArraySize
(samples);
if
(!summary.validation_complete || count <
1
||
      count !=
ArraySize
(results) || count != summary.total)
     {
      error =
"Incomplete batch or inconsistent sample/result sizes."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
   SDoubleBottomBatchSummary counted;
   InitDoubleBottomBatchSummary(counted);
for
(
int
i =
0
; i < count; i++)
     {
if
(results[i].execution_error ||
         !CountDoubleBottomBatchStatus(results[i].status, counted))
        {
         error =
"Batch contains an execution error or unknown status."
;
return
(
false
);
        }
     }
if
(counted.invalid_count != summary.invalid_count ||
      counted.candidate_count != summary.candidate_count ||
      counted.confirmed_count != summary.confirmed_count ||
      counted.failed_count != summary.failed_count)
     {
      error =
"Batch counters do not match result rows."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
return
(
true
);
  }
The UTF-8 payload is written in binary mode so the number of bytes written can be checked directly. FileFlush() and FileClose() return no Boolean result; error diagnostics and a complete readback provide the export checks.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Writes the complete UTF-8 payload and checks byte count and flush|
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
WriteDoubleBottomBatchBytes(
const
int
handle,
uchar
&bytes[],
const
int
count,
string
&error)
  {
ResetLastError
();
uint
written =
FileWriteArray
(handle, bytes,
0
, count);
int
code =
GetLastError
();
if
(written != (
uint
)count || code !=
0
)
     {
      error =
"Report write failed. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(code);
return
(
false
);
     }
ResetLastError
();
FileFlush
(handle);
   code =
GetLastError
();
if
(code !=
0
)
     {
      error =
"Report flush failed. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(code);
return
(
false
);
     }
return
(
true
);
  }
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Reopens the closed file and compares every byte with the payload |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
VerifyDoubleBottomBatchFile(
const
string
path,
uchar
&expected[],
const
int
count,
string
&error)
  {
ResetLastError
();
int
handle =
FileOpen
(path,
FILE_READ
|
FILE_BIN
);
if
(handle ==
INVALID_HANDLE
)
     {
      error =
"Cannot reopen report for verification. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(
GetLastError
());
return
(
false
);
     }
uchar
actual[];
bool
ok =
FileSize
(handle) == (
ulong
)count;
if
(ok)
      ok =
ArrayResize
(actual, count) == count;
if
(ok)
      ok =
FileReadArray
(handle, actual,
0
, count) == (
uint
)count;
FileClose
(handle);
if
(ok)
     {
for
(
int
i =
0
; i < count; i++)
        {
if
(actual[i] != expected[i])
           {
            ok =
false
;
break
;
           }
        }
     }
if
(!ok)
      error =
"Report byte verification failed."
;
return
(ok);
  }
The writer constructs the three marked sections, verifies the temporary file and publishes a separate report. The payload and verification buffer are held in memory, so report size contributes to memory use. The function does not claim crash-safe atomic persistence.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Writes and verifies a separate report for this completed batch   |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
SaveDoubleBottomBatchSummary(SPatternSample &samples[],
                                  SDoubleBottomValidation &results[],
const
SDoubleBottomSettings &settings,
                                  SDoubleBottomBatchSummary &summary,
string
&error)
  {
   summary.report_file =
""
;
if
(!CheckDoubleBottomSettings(settings, error) ||
      !CheckDoubleBottomBatchRows(samples, results, summary, error) ||
      !PrepareDoubleBottomSummaryFolder(error))
return
(
false
);
//--- Mark each CSV section and record the contracts needed for comparison
string
report =
"SECTION,SUMMARY\r\n"
;
   report +=
"REPORT_SCHEMA,VALIDATOR_REVISION,SAMPLE_FORMAT,BATCH_TIME,TIME_BASIS,PATTERN_TYPE,TOTAL,INVALID,CANDIDATE,CONFIRMED,FAILED\r\n"
;
   report += DOUBLE_BOTTOM_REPORT_SCHEMA +
","
+ DOUBLE_BOTTOM_VALIDATOR_REVISION +
",2,"
+
TimeToString
(summary.generated_at,
TIME_DATE
|
TIME_SECONDS
) +
",LAST_KNOWN_SERVER_TIME_AFTER_VALIDATION,DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE,"
+
IntegerToString
(summary.total) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(summary.invalid_count) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(summary.candidate_count) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(summary.confirmed_count) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(summary.failed_count) +
"\r\n"
;
   report +=
"SECTION,SETTINGS\r\n"
;
   report +=
"PIVOT_STRENGTH,MIN_LOW_SEPARATION,MAX_LOW_DIFFERENCE_PCT,MIN_DEPTH_PCT,MIN_SYMMETRY_PCT,BREAKOUT_BUFFER_PCT,FAILURE_TOLERANCE_PCT\r\n"
;
   report +=
IntegerToString
(settings.pivot_strength) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(settings.min_low_separation) +
","
+
             DoubleBottomBatchNumber(settings.max_low_difference_pct) +
","
+
             DoubleBottomBatchNumber(settings.min_depth_pct) +
","
+
             DoubleBottomBatchNumber(settings.min_symmetry_pct) +
","
+
             DoubleBottomBatchNumber(settings.breakout_buffer_pct) +
","
+
             DoubleBottomBatchNumber(settings.failure_tolerance_pct) +
"\r\n"
;
   report +=
"SECTION,RESULTS\r\n"
;
   report +=
"SAMPLE_ID,SYMBOL,TIMEFRAME_INT,START_TIME,END_TIME,BARS,STATUS,SCORE,FIRST_LOW_INDEX,SECOND_LOW_INDEX,NECKLINE_INDEX,BREAKOUT_INDEX,FAILURE_INDEX,SEPARATION_BARS,FIRST_LOW_PRICE,SECOND_LOW_PRICE,NECKLINE_PRICE,PATTERN_DEPTH,DEPTH_PCT,LOW_DIFFERENCE_PCT,SYMMETRY_PCT,RECOVERY_PCT,REASON\r\n"
;
for
(
int
i =
0
; i <
ArraySize
(samples); i++)
     {
//--- Serialize stored values without querying the active chart or symbol
SPatternSample sample = samples[i];
      SDoubleBottomValidation result = results[i];
      report +=
IntegerToString
(sample.id) +
","
+ QuoteDoubleBottomBatchCsvField(sample.symbol) +
","
+
IntegerToString
((
int
)sample.timeframe) +
","
+
TimeToString
(sample.start_time,
TIME_DATE
|
TIME_SECONDS
) +
","
+
TimeToString
(sample.end_time,
TIME_DATE
|
TIME_SECONDS
) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(sample.bars) +
","
+ DoubleBottomStatusToString(result.status) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.score) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.first_low_index) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.second_low_index) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.neckline_index) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.breakout_index) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.failure_index) +
","
+
IntegerToString
(result.separation_bars) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.first_low_price) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.second_low_price) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.neckline_price) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.pattern_depth) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.depth_pct) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.low_difference_pct) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.symmetry_pct) +
","
+
                DoubleBottomBatchNumber(result.recovery_pct) +
","
+
                QuoteDoubleBottomBatchCsvField(result.reason) +
"\r\n"
;
     }
//--- Use a per-run filename and never overwrite an existing report
string
stamp =
TimeToString
(
TimeLocal
(),
TIME_DATE
|
TIME_SECONDS
);
StringReplace
(stamp,
"."
,
""
);
StringReplace
(stamp,
":"
,
""
);
StringReplace
(stamp,
" "
,
"_"
);
string
path = GetPatternFolder(PATTERN_DOUBLE_BOTTOM_CANDIDATE) +
"VALIDATION_SUMMARY_"
+ stamp +
"_"
+
IntegerToString
((
long
)
GetMicrosecondCount
()) +
".csv"
;
string
temporary = path +
".tmp"
;
if
(
FileIsExist
(path) ||
FileIsExist
(temporary))
     {
      error =
"Report filename collision; retry the batch."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
uchar
bytes[];
int
count =
StringToCharArray
(report, bytes,
0
,
WHOLE_ARRAY
,
CP_UTF8
) -
1
;
if
(count <=
0
)
     {
      error =
"Cannot encode report as UTF-8."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
ResetLastError
();
int
handle =
FileOpen
(temporary,
FILE_WRITE
|
FILE_BIN
);
if
(handle ==
INVALID_HANDLE
)
     {
      error =
"Cannot open report file. Check path, permissions, disk and file locks. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(
GetLastError
());
return
(
false
);
     }
bool
ok = WriteDoubleBottomBatchBytes(handle, bytes, count, error);
ResetLastError
();
FileClose
(handle);
int
close_error =
GetLastError
();
if
(close_error !=
0
)
     {
      error =
"Report close diagnostic: "
+
IntegerToString
(close_error);
      ok =
false
;
     }
if
(ok)
      ok = VerifyDoubleBottomBatchFile(temporary, bytes, count, error);
if
(ok)
     {
ResetLastError
();
      ok =
FileMove
(temporary,
0
, path,
0
);
if
(!ok)
         error =
"Cannot publish report. Error: "
+
IntegerToString
(
GetLastError
());
     }
if
(!ok)
     {
if
(
FileIsExist
(temporary) && !
FileDelete
(temporary))

" Temporary file cleanup failed: "
+ temporary;
return
(
false
);
     }
   summary.report_file = path;
   error =
""
;
return
(
true
);
  }
4. Processing the actual collection
The coordinator checks the library and settings, obtains a checked snapshot and allocates a parallel results array. It rejects an empty library and aborts on detected execution failures, unknown statuses or an inconsistent Boolean/status pair. Completed validation is recorded before export begins.
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Validates a copied collection before attempting report export    |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
bool
ValidateDoubleBottomLibrary(CPatternLibrary *
library
,
const
SDoubleBottomSettings &settings,
                                 SDoubleBottomBatchSummary &summary,
string
&error)
  {
   InitDoubleBottomBatchSummary(summary);
if
(
CheckPointer
(
library
) ==
POINTER_INVALID
|| !
library
.IsReady())
     {
      error =
"The pattern library is not available."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
if
(!CheckDoubleBottomSettings(settings, error))
return
(
false
);
   SPatternSample samples[];
if
(!
library
.GetAllSamples(samples))
     {
      error =
"Cannot allocate the sample snapshot."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
   summary.total =
ArraySize
(samples);
if
(summary.total ==
0
)
     {
      error =
"The pattern library does not contain any samples."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
   SDoubleBottomValidation results[];
if
(
ArrayResize
(results, summary.total) != summary.total)
     {
      error =
"Cannot allocate batch results."
;
return
(
false
);
     }
for
(
int
i =
0
; i < summary.total; i++)
     {
if
(
IsStopped
())
        {
         error =
"Batch interrupted before completion."
;
return
(
false
);
        }
bool
accepted = ValidateDoubleBottom(samples[i], settings, results[i]);
if
(results[i].execution_error ||
         accepted != (results[i].status != DOUBLE_BOTTOM_INVALID) ||
         !CountDoubleBottomBatchStatus(results[i].status, summary))
        {
         error =
"Validator execution failed for sample #"
+
IntegerToString
(samples[i].id) +
": "
+ results[i].reason;
return
(
false
);
        }
     }
//--- This is the last known server time, not the report completion time
summary.generated_at =
TimeCurrent
();
   summary.validation_complete =
true
;
return
(SaveDoubleBottomBatchSummary(samples, results, settings, summary, error));
  }
GetAllSamples() returns false when its outer snapshot allocation fails. The validator also checks allocation of its swing-low array and sets execution_error if that allocation fails. These supporting changes are included in PatternLibrary.mqh and DoubleBottomValidator.mqh.
An ordinary false return with
INVALID
and no execution_error remains a reportable rejection, including unsuitable sample input. Invalid settings are rejected before the loop. The execution_error flag identifies the explicitly detected allocation failure; it is not a catch-all handler for terminal termination or every possible runtime failure.
Processing is synchronous. Validation cost grows with the number of samples and possible swing-low pairs, and the interface may pause during a large batch. The code checks for a stop request between samples, not inside every pair comparison.

Operating and reviewing the batch
Extract the supplied archive into the terminal's Data Folder. The files are already arranged under
MQL5\Experts\PatternRecorder
and

To run a collection validation:
Attach the Expert Advisor and confirm that Recorded Samples shows the expected library count.
Review the validation inputs in the Expert Advisor properties. These are the settings that will be written into the report.
Keep the source samples and validator package used for the run so the exported results can be compared later.

The batch can be launched from any chart because it evaluates stored candle arrays. To inspect a result visually, first use a chart matching its stored symbol and timeframe. Then use
VIEW SAMPLES

VALIDATE SELECTED
with the same settings, and choose
SHOW ON CHART
. A chart change can reinitialize the EA, so validation must follow that change.
Reading the summary CSV
Confirm the batch header and settings
When opening the file, first verify the batch row and settings section. The status values must be read together with the pivot, separation, depth, low-difference, symmetry, breakout, and failure settings that produced them.
TOTAL
should equal the result-row count and the sum of the four status counts. The writer checks these relationships before export and compares the saved bytes with the intended payload. Counter agreement alone cannot detect every altered value, and these checks do not protect a report from edits made after saving.
The result rows can then be sorted by status or sample ID. Sorting by score is useful within accepted structures, but INVALID rows should not be ranked as though a zero score represented weak accepted geometry. For an invalid result, the reason field is the important output.
What each status means in the report
INVALID
means that the validator did not retain a pair under the active mandatory rules. The sample may contain too few complete candles, fewer than two qualifying swing lows or swing lows whose pairs fail separation, depth, low-difference or symmetry requirements. The reason narrows the path, while individual chart review helps determine whether the stored label or the rule definition deserves attention.
CANDIDATE
means an accepted pair was found, but the stored interval ended without the first decisive close crossing either outcome level. It is not a prediction that confirmation will occur later. It describes the evidence available inside that sample boundary.
CONFIRMED
means a candle closed above the calculated breakout level before a failure close occurred.
BREAKOUT_INDEX
identifies the first such candle. The row retains the same selected lows and neckline used to calculate the score.
FAILED
means the structure passed its mandatory geometry but a candle closed below the failure level before breakout.
FAILURE_INDEX
identifies that first decisive close. A failed record is not useless data; it shows acceptable shape without the desired outcome and is important when studying whether geometry alone is informative.
Tracing a row back to the chart
SAMPLE_ID
connects a summary row to
SAMPLE_<ID>.csv
and to the panel list. Symbol, timeframe, and dates provide a second identity check. The stored indices are array positions inside that sample, not shifts on the current chart.
For an accepted row, begin with
FIRST_LOW_INDEX, SECOND_LOW_INDEX
, and
NECKLINE_INDEX
. Their separation and prices describe the selected geometry.
DEPTH_PCT, LOW_DIFFERENCE_PCT, SYMMETRY_PCT
, and
RECOVERY_PCT
explain the score's components. The decisive index then distinguishes a candidate from a confirmed or failed result.
If a row looks surprising, do not edit the summary to make it agree with the manual label. Open the source sample, run individual validation with the same settings and show it on the matching chart. This returns the reported indices to the candles from which they were calculated.
Status counts do not measure profitability. The sample format does not store entry, spread, stops, exits, or realized return. The batch report therefore cannot estimate trading performance.
For the trader, this process makes it easier to move from the overall distribution to a specific candidate, confirmation, failure, or rejection. For the developer, the CSV exposes the exact indices and measurements returned by the validator, while the chart reviewer confirms how those values map to candles.

Validating the stored collection

Requiring individual validation before chart review

This demonstrated that completing a batch does not provide a retained individual result for chart review. A sample must be selected and validated before its structure can be displayed.

Scope of the results
The recordings and exported files demonstrate processing of the 12-record collection, inclusion of H4 samples from an M30 chart, consistent totals across repeated runs, preservation of separate reports, and agreement with individual validation for two samples. They also demonstrate that batch results cannot be used directly for chart rendering.
The collection contained one symbol and produced
INVALID
and
CONFIRMED
results only. These recordings do not demonstrate
CANDIDATE
or
FAILED
classifications, an empty library, invalid settings, file-operation failures, unavailable symbols or large-library performance. Exact chart-object coordinates and trading performance were not evaluated.
Conclusion
Individual validation explains one stored double-bottom sample. Part 86 adds the missing collection view. One panel action now applies the unchanged validator to every sample held by the library, counts
INVALID
,
CANDIDATE
,
CONFIRMED
, and
FAILED
outcomes, and writes a detailed CSV report.
The report records its time basis, schema and validator revision, active settings, sample context, selected indices, measurements, score and reason. Original sample files remain untouched. Non-consecutive IDs are handled through the library array, and seventeen-significant-digit serialization preserves numeric values without relying on symbol availability.
The batch report provides a collection view, while its detailed rows remain tied to sample IDs and candle indices. This supports comparison of results under recorded settings. It does not measure trading performance or establish that every stored label represents a valid market formation.
The visual reviewer remains the place to examine a particular formation. The batch report shows which stored samples produced each status and keeps those results available outside the terminal.

for: The report stores the active settings, report schema, sample format and validator revision alongside the results.
The CSV report includes 'SAMPLE_ID, SYMBOL, TIMEFRAME_INT, START_TIME, END_TIME, BARS, STATUS, SCORE, FIRST_LOW_INDEX, SECOND_LOW_INDEX, NECKLINE_INDEX, BREAKOUT_INDEX, FAILURE_INDEX, ... REASON'.
CONFIRMED means a candle closed above the calculated breakout level before a failure close occurred. BREAKOUT_INDEX identifies the first such candle.
FAILED means the structure passed its mandatory geometry but a candle closed below the failure level before breakout. FAILURE_INDEX identifies that first decisive close.
CANDIDATE means an accepted pair was found, but the stored interval ended without the first decisive close crossing either outcome level.

The validator uses explicit mandatory geometry rules: minimum low separation, maximum low difference, minimum depth, minimum symmetry, breakout buffer, and failure tolerance — all configurable and logged with results.
The batch validation uses stored candles (not live chart data), enabling reproducible, time-stamped, out-of-context testing on historical price arrays.
The report retains seventeen significant digits for prices, scores and measurements — preserving exact numerical values for later comparison and backtesting.

non_fatal: Статья описывает инструмент валидации уже зафиксированных паттернов (двойное дно) на исторических данных, но не содержит ни торгового правила входа, ни рыночного признака/фильтра, вычисляемого в реальном времени по закрытым барам — только механизм классификации сохранённых образцов.

Идея основана на анализе статичных, заранее сохранённых наборов свечей (SPatternSample), а не на онлайн-расчёте сигнала по потоку цен — отсутствует описание, как генерировать признак или условие входа в режиме реального времени.

Не указано, как именно вычисляются ключевые элементы паттерна (например, swing lows, neckline, breakout level) в терминах точной формулы по закрытым барам: упоминаются «mandatory geometry rules», «pair search», «pivot strength», но без математического определения — например, нет формулы для определения локального минимума с силой 2, без перерисовки и без будущих баров.

Отсутствует описание целевой переменной или метки для обучения модели (если бы она использовалась): статья не говорит, как формируется label (например, 'breakout occurred within N bars'), а лишь классифицирует уже завершённые интервалы по заданным жёстким правилам.

Нет информации о том, как применять результаты валидации к текущему рынку: не ясно, является ли CONFIRMED-статус триггером для входа, и если да — то по какому ценовому уровню и с каким смещением (например, выше neckline или выше breakout level), и как этот уровень рассчитывается на лету.

judge.summary: Статья описывает архитектуру и реализацию инструмента пакетной валидации уже сохранённых образцов паттерна «двойное дно» на исторических данных, включая формирование CSV-отчётов с детализацией статусов, параметров и метрик. Она не представляет собой торговое правило или рыночный признак, так как не содержит ни детерминированного условия входа, ни формулы вычисления признака по закрытым барам в реальном времени.
